comments: What you say to ATC, and which request each phrase means.
THIS FILE IS THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS AND IS NEVER WRITTEN TO. Editing it works, but
the next update replaces it. To change what you say, use the Voice Commands tab in
the manager, which writes your changes to a separate file:
That file holds only what you changed, so a new release's new commands and corrected
phrasings still reach you. A whole copy of this file in your own folder could not do
that: your edit and an out-of-date default would be indistinguishable.
The leading verb is expanded automatically - 'request taxi' also matches
'requesting taxi', so only one form is listed. Same for report/reporting and
Longest phrase wins, so 'request taxi clearance' beats 'request taxi'. A distress
call wins over anything said in the same breath, whatever the lengths.
Restart listening after any change, so the recogniser rebuilds its grammar.

notes: Three repetitions, which is real procedure and the only form that survived
measurement: the short forms produced 22 false declarations in ten minutes at a
median confidence of 0.92. See docs/FALSE-TRIGGERS-PLAN.md before shortening
Needed because a repeat declaration is deliberately silent: without a way to
cancel, one false mayday would suppress a real one for the rest of the sortie.
